research_brief.title: Harness Definition Package standards and framework research
research_brief.source_policy: Primary or official sources only for load-bearing claims; research papers are identified as preprints where applicable.

confidence_scale.high: Directly supported by a current official specification, standards body page, government publication, release record, or paper landing page.
confidence_scale.moderate: Supported by a primary source, but status or version labeling differs across official surfaces or the source is a living document.
confidence_scale.low: Inference or unresolved status; not used as a normative adoption basis.

sources.subject: Oracle Open Agent Specification
sources.title: Open Agent Specification, Agent Spec - PyAgentSpec 26.1.2 documentation
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Latest stable release documentation; describes a portable, platform-agnostic agent and flow configuration language.
sources.evidence: The page installs pyagentspec==26.1.2, describes Agents and Flows, and identifies Agent Spec as complementary to MCP and A2A.

sources.subject: Oracle Open Agent Specification
sources.title: Agent Spec 26.1.2
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Latest non-draft, non-prerelease GitHub release.
sources.evidence: GitHub release metadata reports tag agent-spec-26.1.2 and publication time 2026-06-02T10:35:07Z.

sources.subject: Oracle Open Agent Specification
sources.title: Agent Spec VERSION at main commit d5633facba93fe3f2c593a70fe05bb8f031a6f49
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Development branch snapshot, not a stable release.
sources.evidence: The VERSION file reads 26.2.0.dev7 at the repository HEAD observed during research.

sources.subject: Oracle Open Agent Specification
sources.title: Open Agent Specification language specification v26.1.0
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Latest released language payload version exposed by the stable documentation.
sources.evidence: Defines Agent Spec components, input/output schemas, agents, flows, tools, MCP, A2A, references, serialization, and sensitive fields.

sources.subject: Oracle create-agent-spec skill
sources.title: create-agent-spec/SKILL.md at agent-spec-26.1.2
sources.version_or_revision: Bundled in Agent Spec 26.1.2; file SHA aa1b5b7489158e9f61efd2a623bfde681d3989cd
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Released repository skill, not part of the normative Agent Spec language.
sources.evidence: The skill requires constructing artifacts through PyAgentSpec SDK objects, SDK export, round-trip validation, secret exclusion, and confirmation for side-effecting tools.

sources.subject: Agent Spec Eval
sources.title: Open Agent Specification Evaluation (Agent Spec Eval)
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Released extension and Python SDK subpackage.
sources.evidence: Defines datasets, metrics, evaluators, results, aggregators, repetition/ensembles, concurrency control, and sensitive evaluation data guidance.

sources.subject: Agent Spec Tracing
sources.title: Open Agent Specification Tracing (Agent Spec Tracing)
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Released extension; development documentation continues to evolve.
sources.evidence: Defines traces, spans, events, processors, standard agent/flow/tool/LLM events, correlation identifiers, and sensitive-field handling.

sources.subject: JSON Schema
sources.title: JSON Schema Draft 2020-12
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Current published JSON Schema version; a separate latest snapshot remains work in progress.
sources.evidence: The official page identifies Draft 2020-12, its core and validation specifications, meta-schema, vocabularies, and publication date.

sources.subject: Agent Skills
sources.title: Agent Skills Specification
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Open format with no GitHub releases or tags observed; the metadata version example is not a specification version.
sources.evidence: Requires a SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter and Markdown body; defines required name and description and optional scripts, references, assets, and experimental allowed-tools.

sources.subject: Model Context Protocol
sources.title: Model Context Protocol Specification 2026-07-28
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Current released protocol revision.
sources.evidence: The date-versioned specification defines the modern stateless protocol core, capability discovery, tools/resources/prompts, authorization, transports, and JSON Schema usage.

sources.subject: Model Context Protocol
sources.title: The 2026-07-28 Specification
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: General release announcement; all four Tier 1 SDKs reported as supporting the revision.
sources.evidence: Announces the released revision and documents breaking changes including stateless operation, MRTR, header routing, caching, authorization changes, extensions, and deprecations.

sources.subject: Agent2Agent Protocol
sources.title: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol Specification
sources.version_or_revision: Protocol 1.0; page labels latest released version 1.0.0
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Stable 1.0 protocol family; patch numbers do not affect protocol compatibility negotiation.
sources.evidence: Defines agent discovery, Agent Cards, tasks/messages/artifacts, multiple protocol bindings, streaming, push notifications, security, and version negotiation.

sources.subject: Agent2Agent Protocol
sources.title: A2A v1.0.1
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Latest repository release; contains specification bug fixes while the negotiated wire version remains 1.0.
sources.evidence: Release notes identify HTTP binding, transcoding error, and TaskStatus fixes.

sources.subject: OpenAPI
sources.title: OpenAPI Specification v3.2.0
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Latest published OpenAPI Specification.
sources.evidence: Defines a language-agnostic HTTP API description; the normative text is authoritative over its informational JSON Schema.

sources.subject: Open Agentic Schema Framework
sources.title: Open Agent Schema Framework (OASF)
sources.version_or_revision: Documentation for the living OASF project
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Active open-source schema framework for agent records, capabilities, skills, domains, modules, and locators.
sources.evidence: Describes OASF as an extensible data model for agent attributes, skills, capabilities, and discovery across A2A, MCP, and related systems.

sources.subject: Open Agentic Schema Framework
sources.title: OASF Release v1.1.0
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Latest non-prerelease GitHub release.
sources.evidence: Adds more granular skills/domains, category and class API improvements, descriptor and module artifact fields, and stronger generated JSON Schema constraints.

sources.subject: Open Agentic Schema Framework
sources.title: Creating an Agent Record
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Current guide, but its examples lag the v1.1.0 repository release.
sources.evidence: Defines record identity, semantic version, schema version, skills, domains, locators, modules, and Draft-07 validation guidance.

sources.subject: Requirements engineering
sources.title: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 Systems and software engineering - Life cycle processes - Requirements engineering
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Published and current after confirmation in 2024; stage 90.92 indicates it is to be revised and a committee draft is under development.
sources.evidence: Specifies requirements-engineering processes, required information items, their contents, and format guidance across system/software life cycles.

sources.subject: AI risk management and TEVV
sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Current published framework, voluntary and use-case agnostic; NIST states that AI RMF 1.0 is being revised.
sources.evidence: Organizes risk management around Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage and integrates TEVV actors and tasks throughout the AI life cycle.

sources.subject: AI risk management and TEVV
sources.title: AI Risk Management Framework
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: NIST explicitly says AI RMF 1.0 is being revised.
sources.evidence: Provides the current status and links to the RMF, Playbook, Roadmap, Crosswalk, and Generative AI Profile.

sources.subject: Generative AI risk management
sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Published cross-sectoral companion profile for AI RMF 1.0.
sources.evidence: Focuses on governance, content provenance, pre-deployment testing, incident disclosure, and suggested actions for GAI risks.

sources.subject: AI TEVV
sources.title: NIST AI Resource Center
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Current resource center for operationalizing AI RMF and supporting AI test, evaluation, verification, and validation.
sources.evidence: States that AIRC provides technical resources, tools, and guidance for TEVV of AI.

sources.subject: Assurance cases
sources.title: Structured Assurance Case Metamodel Specification Version 2.3
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Latest formal version listed by OMG, with normative PDF and machine-readable XML.
sources.evidence: OMG lists version 2.3, adoption date October 2023, formal specification, and normative machine-readable SACM XML.

sources.subject: Natural-language harnesses
sources.title: Natural-Language Agent Harnesses
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Research preprint; not a standard and no peer-reviewed venue is stated on the primary record.
sources.evidence: Introduces editable Natural-Language Agent Harnesses and an Intelligent Harness Runtime that interprets policies into calls, handoffs, state updates, validation gates, and artifact contracts.

sources.subject: Harness engineering research
sources.title: Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Research preprint; not a standard.
sources.evidence: Proposes component, experience, and decision observability and treats each harness edit as a falsifiable contract checked against later outcomes.

sources.subject: Harness engineering research
sources.title: Code as Agent Harness
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Research survey preprint; not a standard.
sources.evidence: Frames code as the operational substrate for agent interfaces, planning, memory, tool use, feedback, verification, and multi-agent coordination and identifies open evaluation and oversight problems.

sources.subject: Harness engineering research
sources.title: From Prompts to Contracts: Harness Engineering for Auditable Enterprise LLM Agents
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Research preprint with linked reference implementation and evaluation artifacts; not a standard.
sources.evidence: Places deterministic behavior in code, manifests, schemas, and validation artifacts and evaluates source, routing, trace, output-hygiene, and recommendation-language contracts with fault injection and model substitution.

sources.subject: Harness engineering research
sources.title: Model or Harness? An Interaction-Centric Taxonomy for Localizing Agent Failures
sources.status_as_of_2026_08_12: Research preprint; not a standard.
sources.evidence: Defines 41 failure modes across interactions among model, harness, user, tools, memory, environment, and grader to assign repair responsibility.
